text: Go with custom tooling: ccw-owned peer messaging over its HTTP API replaces native SendMessage/ListAgents for ccw sessions and works across containers, nodes and clusters; native Unix-socket messaging is dropped because sockets do not cross nodes, even on RWX CephFS.

Opt-in peers config section, default disabled, zero behaviour change when off; keys enabled, name (default hostname), advertise_url (default http://<hostname>:<server port>), token (required when enabled, normally ${CCW_PEER_TOKEN}, refuse to start without it, never logged, redacted), directory (default /peers, may be RWX), heartbeat_seconds, stale_seconds, max_message_bytes, inbox_max.

Built-ins off when enabled: CLAUDE_CODE_HARBOR_KITE=0 in the session env, permissions.deny SendMessage and ListAgents in the ccw-written settings.json, and the PreToolUse tool gate denies SendMessage/ListAgents with reason 'use mcp__ccw__send_message / mcp__ccw__peers'.

The ccw MCP server gains peers (optional instance filter; live peers excluding the caller, address <instance>/<session id>, plus name and cwd) and send_message ({to, message, notify_when_idle?}; returns msg_id or a clear error: unknown peer, peer unreachable, too large, inbox full); both only registered when peers.enabled; main agent only like the command tool; the agent instructions get a short paragraph about them when enabled.

Discovery is plain JSON files <directory>/<instance>/<session id>.json {instance, session_id, name, cwd, url, started_at, heartbeat_at}, written atomically on create, refreshed every heartbeat_seconds, removed on destroy/shutdown; live when heartbeat_at is within stale_seconds (no socket probes); ccw removes its own stale entries at startup; no static peer list, no ccw-to-ccw listing API.

POST /v1/peers/messages on the target instance, authenticated by the peer token only (constant-time compare; server.auth_token not accepted there and the peer token not accepted elsewhere), body {from, to_session, message, msg_id, notify_when_idle}; 202 queued, 401, 404 unknown session, 413 too large, 429 inbox full; only mounted when enabled; plus POST /v1/peers/notices with the same auth; body size capped before parse.

Per-session inbox: an idle session gets the message as a turn now, a busy one as a new turn after the current turn completes (never typed into a busy PTY, never mid-turn), in arrival order, framed as <agent-message from=... msg_id=...> with a line telling the agent to reply with mcp__ccw__send_message; SSE events peer_message_received, peer_message_sent, peer_message_delivered and metrics counters; the EVENT_TYPES pin in tests/test_event_log.py updated.

notify_when_idle: when the turn that handled a message completes, the target ccw POSTs /v1/peers/notices to the sender instance url and the sender ccw delivers it to the sending session as a short <peer-idle-notice from=... msg_id=...> message under the same inbox and delivery rules.
Same-cluster TLS is out of scope for ccw itself (it does not terminate TLS); advertise_url may be https behind an ingress or mesh; the README says so.

Compose example with two ccw services sharing one named peers volume for the directory, a shared CCW_PEER_TOKEN, explicit instance names a and b, one image build; the Dockerfile pre-creates /peers owned by agent uid 1000 so a fresh named volume is writable.

Tests use the fake claude only, only the fake-claude task edits tests/conftest.py, reusing the fake's MCP tool calls; unit tests per module; an in-process test with two ccw services on real HTTP ports sharing a tmp directory proving send, framed receive, reply and notify_when_idle; a docker two-container integration test (scripts plus a mise task run by mise run test:integration in CI) proving the same across containers; real-claude acceptance of the tool schemas is cannotVerify, not a skipped task.

README: setup, addressing, config rows for every new key, every new route documented, trust model (any holder of the peer token can push prompts into bypass-mode agents), cross-node via an RWX directory, the TLS note; examples/*.config.yaml are committed symlinks into src/claude_code_wrapper/data/examples.
Follow the repo CLAUDE.md: test-first, uv run, plain ASCII, no em dashes; tasks of about an hour, at most 8 files.
